_note: Sector conditions for the simulation: causes, not outcomes. Drawn from The Western Front Companion (pp. 202-221) and Middlebrook; numbers are judgement where the sources give only a description (see 'why'). Times in minutes after zero (07:30); null = did not attack. Depths in metres from the British front line.

VII Corps.why: Gommecourt: strong German artillery untouched by counter-battery; 'triple barrage' on the 46th; once the North Midland attack failed the barrage was kept on no man's land, cutting the London men off from bombs and reinforcements

VIII Corps.why: German batteries undamaged; defensive barrage on no man's land and British trenches

X Corps.why: 26th Reserve Division, eight battalions, strong guns

XV Corps.why: Intense bombardment from 06:25 including French guns

XIII Corps.why: French heavy artillery and counter-battery; 'attackers heavily outnumbered the defending German infantry'

46th (North Midland) Division.why: Dense smoke disorientated the 137th Brigade; enfilade from the Z; follow-up waves caught by barrage

56th (London) Division.why: Wire mostly well cut; bombardment damaged dugout entrances so the garrison was slow to get out; leading companies formed up on tape in no man's land

31st Division.why: Seemingly undamaged enemy; hurricane of artillery and machine-gun fire

4th Division.why: Wire well cut but deep bunkers untouched; VIII Corps heavy artillery lifted off the front line at 07:20

29th Division.why: Considerable uncut wire; Hawthorn mine at 07:20 warned the Germans; heavy artillery lifted at 07:20

36th (Ulster) Division.why: German wire well cut; 109th Brigade and the 108th south of the Ancre crept to within 100 yards from Thiepval Wood before the lift (the 108th north of the river did not, and was stopped); objectives to the second line by 10:10

32nd Division.why: Thiepval's cellars sheltered machine-gun crews; 17th HLI crept to within 30-40 yards of the Leipzig Salient

8th Division.why: Long approach up Mash Valley; flanking fire from Ovillers, La Boisselle and the Thiepval spur

34th Division.why: Lochnagar and Y Sap mines; flanking fire from Schwaben Höhe and Sausage Redoubt; Tyneside Irish advanced at zero from Tara-Usna

21st Division.why: Smoke on the inner flank; Tambour mines

17th (Northern) Division.why: Fricourt strongly fortified with deep bunkers; 7th Green Howards' company went at 07:45 by mistake; 7th East Yorks attacked at 14:33 after a weak bombardment

18th (Eastern) Division.why: Creeping barrage; Russian saps and Stokes hurricane bombardment; Kasino Point mine destroyed a machine-gun post

30th Division.why: Wire well cut; creeping barrage; French heavy artillery; 90th Brigade advanced on Montauban at 08:30

germanReserves.why: Local reserves counter-attack within hours; regimental and divisional reserves (e.g. Bavarian RIR 8 at the Schwaben Redoubt) arrive from the afternoon; at Gommecourt the 2nd Guard Reserve Division's reserves counter-attacked the London Division from three sides once the North Midland attack had failed (judgement on numbers)
